Title revised: Arrested but Unstoppable / 체포됐지만 멈추지 않는 사도들
paragraphs: While Peter and John were still talking to the crowd, the priests showed up with the chief of the Temple police and some Sadducees — and they were furious. These rookie apostles were teaching the people and announcing that, in Jesus, resurrection from the dead had actually happened. So they arrested Peter and John and locked them up overnight, since it was already late. But many who heard the message had already believed — roughly five thousand people!

The next day, Jerusalem's power players called a meeting: the rulers, the religious leaders, the scholars, plus Annas the Chief Priest, Caiaphas, John, Alexander — basically everyone who was anyone. They put Peter and John in the middle of the room and grilled them: "Who put you in charge here? What gives you the right to do this?"

Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, let them have it: "Rulers and leaders of the people — if we're on trial today for helping a sick man, if you're investigating this healing, then I'll be totally upfront: we have nothing to hide. By the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth — the One you killed on a cross, the One God raised from the dead — by his name this man stands before you healthy and whole. Jesus is 'the stone you builders threw out, which has now become the cornerstone.' There is no other way to be saved; no other name has been or ever will be given to us by which we can be saved. Only this one."

They couldn't take their eyes off them — Peter and John standing there so confident, so sure of themselves! And it got even more fascinating when they realized these two were ordinary guys with no Scripture training or formal education. They recognized them as companions of Jesus — but with the healed man standing right in front of them, standing so straight, so completely healed — what could they possibly say against that?

So they sent Peter and John out of the room to figure out a plan. They huddled up: "What are we supposed to do with these men? By now the whole town knows a miracle happened, and that they're behind it. We can't deny that. But to keep it from spreading further, let's shut them down with threats so they won't dare use Jesus' name with anyone ever again."

They called the two back in and warned them never, ever to speak or teach in the name of Jesus again. But Peter and John fired right back: "You decide what's right in God's eyes — listening to you, or listening to God? As for us, there's no question: we cannot keep quiet about what we've seen and heard."

The religious leaders threatened them again, then let them go. They couldn't find a single charge that would stick — nothing that would keep them locked up. The people wouldn't have stood for it; everyone was praising God over what had happened. And the man who had been miraculously healed was over forty years old.

As soon as Peter and John were released, they went straight to their friends and reported everything the high priests and religious leaders had said. Hearing the report, they all lifted their voices together in a beautiful harmony of prayer: "Strong God, you made heaven and earth and sea and everything in them. By the Holy Spirit you spoke through your servant, our father David: 'Why the big noise, nations? Why the mean plots, peoples? Earth's leaders push for position, rulers meet for summit talks — the God-deniers, the Messiah-defiers!'"

"And that's exactly what happened — they really did meet: Herod and Pontius Pilate, along with nations and peoples, even Israel itself! They met right here in this city to plot against your holy Son Jesus, the One you made Messiah, carrying out the plans you set in motion long ago."

"And now they're at it again! Lord, take note of their threats, and give your servants fearless confidence to preach your message — as you stretch out your hand to heal, and do miracles and wonders in the name of your holy servant Jesus."
While they prayed, the building where they met shook. Every one of them was filled with the Holy Spirit and went on speaking God's Word with bold, fearless confidence.

The entire family of believers was united — one heart, one soul! They didn't treat their belongings as private property. Nobody said, "That's mine — hands off." Everything was shared. The apostles gave powerful testimony to the resurrection of the Master Jesus, and God's grace rested richly on them all.

And so it turned out that not a single person among them was needy. Those who owned fields or houses sold them, brought the money from the sale to the apostles, and offered it up. The apostles then distributed it to each person according to need.
There was Joseph — the apostles nicknamed him "Barnabas," meaning "Son of Encouragement" — a Levite from Cyprus. He sold a field he owned and laid the money at the apostles' feet.
title: Arrested but Unstoppable
